**Key findings from the logger implementation:**

1. `createLogFunction(clack.log.error, console.error, CLI_COLORS.error)` — the error log function has `CLI_COLORS.error` (i.e. `picocolors.red`) baked in as its third argument, meaning it automatically applies red coloring to the message text before passing to clack. So calling `logger.error(CLI_COLORS.error('Smoke tests failed.'))` pre-colors the string red, and then the logger colors it red again — double ANSI codes.

2. `createLogFunction(clack.log.step, console.log)` — `step` has no built-in color function, so the `CLI_COLORS.success(...)` wrapper on line 314 is the only styling applied. No double-coloring issue here.

3. `logger.outro('')` — clack's outro draws the closing visual delimiter (a bottom border line) for an interactive CLI session. Calling it unconditionally means failure runs also emit this closing border after the stack traces, which looks odd.

4. `problems.length > 0` is evaluated in two separate places.
